story.headline: University of Washington team uses AI to design protein-cutting enzymes from scratch
story.summary: Researchers led by David Baker at the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design report in two Nature papers published Oct. 14 that they used AI tools to design proteases, enzymes that cut proteins at chosen sites, from scratch. Of 135 zinc-based designs tested, 36% cut their target peptides, and 13 of 69 cysteine-based designs worked, according to the papers.

quote.text: To see if it could be done, David Baker at the University of Washington and his colleagues combined several advanced artificial intelligence tools to create both cysteine and zinc proteases.
